newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bonds stay vulnerable to downturn.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bonds stay vulnerable to downturn.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures will likely stay vulnerable to quick downturns, particularly after low-volume bounces, going into Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, analysts said.

"I feel like today and Monday are sort of like the Twilight Zone before the FOMC meeting," said Matthew Crosson, director of fixed income Pegasus Econometrics Group. "I think the market...will be vulnerable to sudden reversals."
"New money is going to be on the sidelines," he added, warning about the likely thin nature of up moves before the FOMC meeting.

September T-bond futures, which in the past few days had been grinding back up after big losses in the previous week, tumbled to a low of 112-27/32 in early trade from an overnight high of 113-27/32. They ended at 113-20/32 on Thursday.
The contract had since drifted back up slightly to the mid-113s by mid-morning.

"The market the last two weeks has had a very strong tendency of having very high-volume down days and very choppy, low-volume up days," noted Michael Krauss, chief technical strategist at Chase Securities Inc.

He said the market overnight had struck resistance from a gap formed last Friday on the daytime-only chart. He added that the quality of a rally would determine whether the market could break above that gap from 113-27/32 to 114-5/32.
"Volume is key. If you get some bigger volume, probably associated with some good news, and close above that gap, I think you can get up to 115-6/32," he said.

But Krauss was basically anticipating range-trading for a while, supported by some short-term positive factors in the mid-112 area but capped by medium-term bearishness. He said the market could test the 110-handle over the next few weeks.

Crosson saw the 114-11/32, 114-12/32 area as key resistance. An ascending trendline that was broken during the August 8 nosedive and now acting as resistance came in at 114-11/32 today, and 114-12/32 was the August 8 high.
He said the three-day relative strength index (RSI) on the 120-minute chart was climbing out of oversold territory after plunging to single digits, offering some short-term support.
But he added that the dollar's weakness has been an important factor in the bond market's recent losses and that the market would probably stay nervous about the currency in the near term.
